articles.title: ‘I created my mom and talk to her’: AI ghosts and deathslop are changing the way we mourn
articles.summary: The rise of AI-generated tributes and bots for ‘talking’ to the dead has experts concerned more people will grieve in isolation. Tributes rolled in after the death of Dolly Parton last month. Jack White performed Jolene at a London gig.
body: Run Jolene, at just under five minutes, is an earworm of a country song, containing all the cliches of the genre: twangy singer, banjo licks, corny lyrics. Those lyrics concern Jolene, the fictional romantic rival made infamous by Parton. “Somebody better warn Jolene / Dolly’s coming through those gates,” the voice croons. “Run Jolene / Girl you better move your feet.”

The accompanying video depicts Parton, clad in a bedazzled white jumpsuit, hunting down Jolene, a busty redhead with prom curls. Heaven is filled with deceased celebrities who watch on in horror – or amusement – as Jolene bounces from cloud to cloud, or books it up marble staircases, trying to hide from Dolly. Onlookers include the late Michael Jackson, Whitney Houston and Kenny Rogers, as well as Cher, who is still very much alive.
points: The rise of AI-generated tributes and bots for ‘talking’ to the dead has experts concerned more people will grieve in isolation.

articles.title: Fast, furious and potentially fatal: why are supercars suddenly so popular?
articles.summary: Once the preserve of the ultra-rich, supercars are finding new drivers through rentals, finance deals, influencer culture and the manosphere. But why would anyone want a 200mph vehicle?
body: Many of the supercars apprehended by the Met in August bore Middle Eastern number plates. It has been a growing trend for car owners from the region to spend summer in London, bringing their cars with them (at a cost of £25,000 upwards). The orange Lamborghini that Tatman seized had Dubai plates. Most of the vehicle owners retrieved their cars the next day after paying fines and presenting the correct paperwork. The Lamborghini driver was subsequently seen driving respectfully and not revving his engine. Lessons were learned, although the question remains: why ship a 200mph car to London to drive in a 20mph zone?

articles.title: Can you freeze leftover risotto? | Kitchen aide
articles.summary: It’s probably not a good idea to freeze cooked risotto rice, but if you must, we have three experts who can tell you how to minimise the mush. I have tried various ways to reheat risotto after freezing, but it always turns into a gloopy, starchy, unappetising mess. What am I doing wrong?
body: And, says Randall, if Jill “really has to freeze leftover risotto”, he would urge her to turn it into arancini instead: “Those work quite well, because you’ve encased the cooked rice in flour, egg wash and breadcrumbs, so moisture doesn’t penetrate the grains.”

And if Jill still wants to batch-cook, Poppy O’Toole suggests a shift in mindset: “The kind of rice that you can freeze would be baked [basmati] rice,” says the author of The Actually Delicious Batch Cookbook, namechecking a spicy chicken number that appeared in Feast a few weeks back. “That freezes and reheats beautifully.” Of course, the freezer is a fan of plain rice, too: “That’s a better way to batch-cook rice,” O’Toole says. “Freezing and reheating risotto never truly works.”

articles.title: Premature review – sunny charm provides screwball energy for surprise-pregnancy comedy
articles.summary: First-time director Kevin Walls creates a film sweet-natured enough to cancel out some comedy misfires as flatmates Eilidh and Cameron prepare for parenthood. The pram in the hallway is the enemy of good art, or so the famous quote goes.
body: Elle Watson is artist Eilidh, who works as a barista in a museum cafe. She has a friends-with-benefits setup with her flatmate Cameron (James Rottger); he has a job in finance and, after two degrees, a mountain of student debt and years in a mind-numbing entry-level position, he’s finally lined up an interview for his dream job. It would be crazy to have the baby, but Eilidh doesn’t take the abortion tablets. She can’t give Cameron a coherent reason why not; fair enough, it’s her decision, a gut feeling. Walls sensibly doesn’t go anywhere near the pro-choice/anti-abortion debate.

But it is a shame his script seems to naturally click more with Cameron’s point of view as he agonises about how a baby will impact his career. Eilidh cheerfully breezes through pregnancy – though inexplicably she turns mumzilla in one scene, demanding that Cameron help her break into a house to steal a secondhand cot, wearing tights over their heads. It’s a scene that reduces the film’s IQ and likability by about 10%. Elsewhere, there are some moments of gentleness, like Cameron’s lovely dad and his no-nonsense wisdom. “Life doesn’t give two shits about your plans, son.”
points: First-time director Kevin Walls creates a film sweet-natured enough to cancel out some comedy misfires as flatmates Eilidh and Cameron prepare for parenthood.

articles.summary: A.P.C.’s 37-piece collection spanning stripey tees, rigid denim jean jackets and miniskirts, and the sine qua non of cargo jackets hits Gap.com this Friday.
body: The 37-piece collection spanning stripey tees, rigid denim jean jackets and miniskirts, and the sine qua non of cargo jackets hits Gap’s e-comm site this Friday.

Catherine Deneuve, Kid Cudi, Katie Holmes. Sacai, Nike, Brain Dead. There’s no end to the people and labels that A.P.C. has collaborated with over the years, but none ever got founder Jean Touitou going quite like his new hookup with Gap.

French fashion’s most unfiltered idealist, Touitou is on a Zoom call from Paris with wife and creative collaborator Judith by his side, and he couldn’t sound more chuffed if he tried. “This is always what I wanted to do,” he declares. “A broader audience—this has always been my dream. Of course, I love our audience, and I wouldn’t be here without them, but it’s a real moment of pleasure to at last come to this reality.”

articles.title: Bella Hadid on Collecting Jewelry, Fall Fashion Musts, and Her New Chopard Gig
articles.summary: The model stars in a new Chopard campaign alongside Liu Wen. We had to ask her about her own jewelry collection—and what else she is shopping for the fall.
body: In the midst of a busy New York Fashion Week, is there a better time to unveil a splashy new supermodel campaign? Chopard certainly seized the moment: Today, the luxury jeweler releases its new Happy Diamonds campaign, starring supermodels Bella Hadid and Liu Wen.

Hadid and Wen sport new pieces that dig into Chopard’s archives—reviving iconic pieces such as its “Happy Sport The First” watch (featuring the loose Happy Diamonds inside the dial), or Happy Diamonds pendant necklaces, featuring three diamonds set in luxurious 18-karat white, rose, or yellow golds.

The jewelry label will also host a party for Wen and Hadid tonight during New York Fashion Week, to celebrate the new campaign. But ahead of all that excitement, Vogue caught up with Hadid earlier this month, to chat about what’s inside her own jewelry collection, what’s on her fall fashion wishlist, and what her next big career moves will be. (Hint: More of her own companies soon—maybe!). Below, read on for our exclusive interview with Hadid.
You have a long history of working with Chopard. What’s been your favorite parts of working with the brand?

articles.title: Sarah Pidgeon Nodded to CBK With Her Sleek Chanel Gown at the 2026 Emmys
articles.summary: The “Love Story” star, who was nominated for an Emmy this year, made reference to Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy’s signature minimalism.
body: Ever since portraying Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy in Ryan Murphy’s Love Story earlier this year, Sarah Pidgeon can not escape fashion comparisons to her famed on-screen character. And it’s no wonder, given that CBK now represents the best of sleek minimalism from the ’90s—a vibe that Pidgeon herself often nails on the red carpet, via her own cool, sleek style choices.

At the 2026 Emmys last night, then, it was only fitting that Pidgeon nodded to CBK once again with her red carpet look —though this time, in a more subtler and more nuanced way. It was a big night for Pidgeon that demanded such a dressing spirit: She was nominated for the role, after all, for lead actress in a limited or anthology series or movie category. “It’s a pinch-me moment,” says Pidgeon. “With Carolyn, I had the challenge of embodying someone who’s so widely known, yet also very mysterious. I think our show offered a real recognition of the powerhouse of a woman that she was.”
points: The “Love Story” star, who was nominated for an Emmy this year, made reference to Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy’s signature minimalism.

articles.title: LA It-Brand High Sport Hits the Gas with New York Fashion Week Teaser
articles.summary: Five years in, founder Alissa Zachary is taking her fashion brand to the next level with a NYFW teaser and an upcoming store opening.
body: Five years after launching High Sport with a pair of $860 cropped kick-flare pants that became one of fashion’s most unlikely cult items, Alissa Zachary is ready for a bigger stage.

For spring 2027, the Los Angeles-based brand will join New York Fashion Week for the first time, releasing a digital lookbook that’s a prelude to what comes next—the runway. It’s a significant milestone for a label that has grown largely through word of mouth, without ever staging a party or press day, let alone a fashion show. And it comes as Zachary is preparing for High Sport’s next phase of growth, including category and retail expansion, creating a physical home for the brand in LA, and eventually, perhaps, taking on outside investment.
“We’re excited to bring the brand to life and bring the community together,” Zachary says. “We have not even scratched the surface, which is exciting, because we have so much potential.”

articles.title: Prince’s Favorite Cheesecake Delivers the Funk
articles.summary: A decade after the rockstar’s death, Vanessa Drews is turning his favorite cheesecake into a Twin Cities sensation.
body: About 20 miles southwest of downtown Minneapolis, in the small town of Excelsior, a curiously named business sits wedged in a strip mall between a taqueria, a nail salon, and a pet groomer.

Wander inside and you might think you’re in a museum dedicated to Prince, the Minneapolis-born musical genius who lived just four miles south of here at his private home and recording studio complex, Paisley Park. The purple walls are dotted with photos of the homegrown superstar, who passed away ten years ago this year. The business may double as a de facto homage to the self-proclaimed “Purple Yoda,” but it’s actually one of the hottest bakeries in the Midwest. Welcome to Cheesecake Funk.

When owner Vanessa Drews opened the cheesecake bakery in September 2025, it quickly became the talk of the baked good-loving Twin Cities. And the Prince connection goes far beyond the bakery’s purple walls. But for lovers of all things sweet and creamy, Cheesecake Funk is today a veritable mecca for those in the know.

articles.title: These Are the Best Power Tools of 2026
articles.summary: I'm a professional woodworker and furniture builder, as well as a DIY home maintenance enthusiast, and these are my favorite tools of 2026 for DIY, woodworking, maintenance, repairs, automotive, garage, and home shop.
body: If you love doing your own home maintenance or tinkering in your garage, having the right tools can make all the difference. If you’re looking for new tools, keeping in mind durability, battery life, and ease of use can help you find something that will work well and save you money down the road on replacing broken tools and worn-out batteries. With so many options, it can be hard to figure out which tools are the best quality, so I put together a list of my favorites to help you choose.

The new Makita 18-volt LXT drill and driver combo set is my favorite tool this year because it has better battery life than other drill and driver sets, and the drill in this kit can deliver 70% more torque than its predecessors, allowing you to drill into tougher materials like pressure-treated lumber or plaster more quickly. The impact driver on this set also has a three-speed control switch, allowing you to choose the amount of force you want to use for a given project. This gives you the advantage of more power when you’re trying to undo an old, rusted nut, and less when you’re trying to screw a hanger into a picture frame.
